record.title: Witsenhausen's conjecture on large spherical sets without orthogonal pairs
record.statement: Let $S^n$ be the unit sphere with its rotation-invariant volume, and let $A\subseteq S^n$ be measurable. Suppose that $A$ contains no two orthogonal vectors. **Witsenhausen's conjecture.** The volume of $A$ is at most twice the volume of two spherical caps of radius $\pi/4$. Witsenhausen proved the weaker bound $\mu(A)\leq 1/(n+1)$; the supplied text does not specify whether the conjecture has been resolved.

record.references:

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2015).

record.title: Pinchasi–Sharir conjecture on planar tangent graphs
record.statement: A tangent graph has one vertex for each disc and an edge when the corresponding discs are tangent. **Pinchasi–Sharir tangent-incidence conjecture.** (i) Planar tangent graphs with $n$ vertices have at most $n^{4/3}\operatorname{polylog}(n)$ edges. (ii) More generally, $m$ red discs and $n$ blue discs, including the special case of $n$ blue points, can touch at most $((mn)^{2/3}+m+n)\operatorname{polylog}(m,n)$ times. The source reports a best known upper bound of $n^{3/2}\log n$ and leaves the conjecture open.

record.title: Haws' regular unimodular triangulation conjecture for matroid polytopes
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid with set of bases $\mathcal{B}$, and let

$$
P(M):=\operatorname{conv}\{e_B:B\in\mathcal{B}\},
$$

where $e_B$ is the sum of the standard basis vectors indexed by $B$. A triangulation is **regular unimodular** when it is induced by a lifting function and every simplex is unimodular. **Haws' conjecture.** For any matroid $M$, the polytope $P(M)$ has a regular unimodular triangulation. The source describes this as a geometric variant of White's algebraic conjecture and gives no resolution.

record.title: The cluster monomial basis conjecture for finite-type LP algebras
record.statement: An LP algebra is an algebra defined from seeds and mutations, and a **cluster monomial** is a product of powers of variables $X_1^{a_1}\dots X_n^{a_n}$ whose variables $X_1,\dots,X_n$ belong to the same seed, with $a_1,\dots,a_n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$. **The cluster monomial basis conjecture.** For any finite-type LP algebra, the set of cluster monomials forms a linear basis of the subring $\mathcal{A}$. This conjecture concerns the linear and combinatorial structure of finite-type LP algebras; the source presents it as a conjecture posed in earlier work and suggests that recursive exchange polynomials may make it easier to verify for product and sum algebras.

record.title: Equality of the absolute Galois group with the dessin automorphism subgroup
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the lattice of biased dessins, let $\Gamma' = \operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{L})$, and let $\Gamma'_0$ be the subgroup of $\Gamma'$ that fixes the three vertices of the bottom element $D_1$. The absolute Galois group $\Gamma$ is a subgroup of $\Gamma'_0$. **Equality conjecture.**

$$
\Gamma = \Gamma'_0.
$$

The preceding theorem establishes the inclusion, while the source states that there is currently no evidence or proof strategy for the reverse inclusion.

record.title: The word-image conjecture for the projective linear group
record.statement:
Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, let $w(x_1,\dots,x_m)$ be a nontrivial group word, and let $\operatorname{PSL}_2(K)$ denote the projective linear group. **Word-image conjecture.** The image of $w$ on $\operatorname{PSL}_2(K)$ is

$$
\operatorname{PSL}_2(K).
$$

This conjecture asks whether every nontrivial word map is surjective on $\operatorname{PSL}_2(K)$. The image is known to contain all non-unipotent elements, while the question of whether the nontrivial unipotent class lies in the image remains open.

record.title: The degree-zero word reformulation for $\operatorname{PSL}_2$
record.statement:
Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, let $w(x_1,\dots,x_m)$ be a group word whose degree in each variable $x_i$ is $0$, and set

$$
G=\operatorname{GL}_2(K)/\{\pm 1\}.
$$

**Degree-zero word reformulation.** The image of $w$ on $G$ must be

$$
\operatorname{PSL}_2(K).
$$

This is presented in the source as a reformulation of the word-image conjecture after reducing to words of degree zero in every variable. It remains open in the stated generality.

record.title: Support bound for higher nim-values in three-pile Sharing Nim
record.statement:
Consider a three-pile Sharing Nim position $(0,a,b)$ with $a\leq b/2$, and let $\mathcal{G}(0,a,b)$ be its nim-value.

**Support-bound conjecture.** If $\mathcal{G}(0,a,b)=g\geq 2$, then

$$
a\leq 2g-1.
$$

This is an empirical estimate based on computations: nim-values $g\geq 2$ appear to be distributed among the bottom $2g$ rows or fewer. The source gives no proof or resolution and notes that the bound may be an overestimate.

record.title: Farhi's three-term representation conjecture for quadratic-floor sequences
record.statement:
Let $a\geq 3$ be an integer, and consider the sequence

$$
\left(\left\lfloor \frac{n^2}{a}\right\rfloor\right)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}.
$$

**Farhi's conjecture.** Every natural number can be represented as the sum of three terms of this sequence.

This conjecture concerns additive representations by a quadratic-floor sequence and is motivated by classical three-square representation results. The paper proves some cases of the conjecture, while the statement in full remains open.
record.source_name: Sebastian Tim Holdum, Frederik Ravn Klausen and Peter Michael Reichstein Rasmussen, “On a Conjecture on the Representation of Positive Integers as the Sum of Three Terms of the Sequence n^2a”, arXiv:1507.00369 (2015).

record.title: Vertex-chromatic-index conjecture for subcubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a subcubic graph, meaning that every vertex of $G$ has degree at most $3$. Let $\chi_{\nu}(G)$ denote the new vertex chromatic number introduced in the paper. **Subcubic vertex-chromatic-index conjecture.**

$$
\chi_{\nu}(G)\le 4.
$$

The conjecture is part of the paper's program of using the new vertex chromatic number to establish acyclic edge-colouring results for Cartesian products. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.

record.title: The 5-connectivity conjecture for block and hole graphs
record.statement: Let $\hat{G}$ be a block and hole graph with one pentagonal block and two quadrilateral holes, or, two quadrilateral blocks and one pentagonal hole. **The 5-connectivity conjecture.** If $\hat{G}$ is $5$-connected, then it is minimally $3$-rigid. record.title: The induced-cycle conjecture for distance-preserving graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A subgraph is **isometric** if distances between its vertices agree with their distances in $G$, and $G$ is **distance preserving** if it has an isometric subgraph of every order from $1$ to $|V(G)|$.

**Induced-cycle conjecture.** If $G$ does not contain an induced cycle of length $5$ or greater, then $G$ is a distance-preserving graph.

This is presented among the paper's questions and conjectures about distance-preserving graphs. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

record.title: The fiber representation conjecture for COMs
record.statement:
A **COM** is a complex of oriented matroids, and an **OM** is an oriented matroid. A **fiber** of a COM is an intersection of its halfspaces. The conjecture is that every COM can be obtained in this way from an OM.

**Fiber representation conjecture.** Every COM is a fiber of some OM.

This would generalize the realizable situation and, together with the Topological Representation Theorem for oriented matroids, give a natural topological representation theorem for COMs. The source presents the claim as open.
record.source_name: Hans-Juergen Bandelt, Victor Chepoi and Kolja Knauer, “COMs: Complexes of Oriented Matroids”, arXiv:1507.06111 (2018).

record.title: The monochromatic path partition conjecture for infinite complete bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Suppose the edges of an infinite complete bipartite graph are coloured with $rin \omega$ colours. Then its vertices can be partitioned into $2r-1$ disjoint monochromatic paths.

**Infinite bipartite monochromatic path conjecture.** The vertices can be partitioned into $2r-1$ disjoint monochromatic paths.

This asks whether the finite-colour path-decomposition result extends from infinite complete graphs to infinite complete bipartite graphs; the statement is presented as an open problem.

record.title: Yan's spanning-tree formula for line graphs of subdivisions
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n+s$ and size $m+s$, in which $s$ vertices have degree $1$ and all other vertices have degree $k$. Let $S(G)$ be the graph obtained by inserting a new vertex into each edge of $G$, let $L(S(G))$ be its line graph, and let $t(H)$ denote the number of spanning trees of a graph $H$. **Yan's conjecture.**

$$
t(L(S(G)))=k^{m+s-n-1}(k+2)^{m-n+1}t(G).
$$

This conjecture extends the known spanning-tree formula for regular graphs to connected graphs with $s$ degree-one vertices and all remaining vertices of degree $k$. The source presents it as a proposed generalization; its status is not established in the supplied text.

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2015).

record.title: Kohl's permutation product conjecture
record.statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $a,b,c$ be integers satisfying $1<a,b,c\leq n-2$. For permutations $x,y\in S_n$, say that they have prescribed orders $a,b,c$ when $x$ has order $a$, $y$ has order $b$, and $xy$ has order $c$. **Kohl's conjecture.** There exist elements $x,y\in S_n$ such that $x$ has order $a$, $y$ has order $b$, and $xy$ has order $c$. The conjecture concerns the existence of permutation triples with prescribed orders and product $1$, equivalently by taking $z=(xy)^{-1}$. The paper's abstract states that this conjecture is proved, so it is solved.

record.title: The 2-way infinite 2-walk conjecture for 3-connected planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $3$-connected $3$-indivisible infinite planar graph. A **$2$-way infinite $2$-walk** is a doubly infinite spanning walk in which every vertex is visited at most twice.

**The 2-way infinite 2-walk conjecture.** The graph $G$ has a $2$-way infinite $2$-walk.

The conjecture is the natural two-ended analogue of the paper's proved one-way result and extends earlier locally finite results by Timar. The text provides no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

record.title: The planar web dimension conjecture for instanton homology
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a web in $\R^{3}$, meaning an embedded trivalent graph, and let $\Jsharp(K)$ be the associated finite-dimensional vector space over the field $\F$ of two elements. A **Tait coloring** of $K$ is an assignment of the colors $\{1,2,3\}$ to its edges such that the three edges incident at every vertex have distinct colors. If $K$ lies in the plane, so that $K\subset\R^{2}\subset\R^{3}$, then **the planar web dimension conjecture** says that

$$
\dim_{\F}\Jsharp(K)=\#\{\text{Tait colorings of }K\}.
$$

The conjecture predicts that, for planar webs, the instanton-homological invariant is determined by the combinatorics of Tait colorings. The paper presents it as plausible evidence-based speculation; no resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: P. B. Kronheimer and T. S. Mrowka, “Tait colorings, and an instanton homology for webs and foams”, arXiv:1508.07205 (2015).
record.references:

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2015).

record.title: Polterovich's conjecture on the nodal-domain ratio
record.statement:
Let $(\phi_n)$ be a sequence of Laplace eigenfunctions, and let $\mu(\phi_n)$ denote the number of nodal domains of $\phi_n$. Let $Sq_1$ be the square of area $1$, with first eigenvalue $\lambda(Sq_1)$. **Polterovich's conjecture.**

$$
\limsup_{n\rightarrow +\infty}\frac{\mu(\phi_n)}{n}\leq \frac{4\pi}{\lambda(Sq_1)}=\frac{2}{\pi}.
$$

The source presents this as a consequence that would follow if suitable bipartite minimal partitions satisfied the stated square-tiling lower bound; it is not established here.

record.title: The middle-level graph conjecture for vertex-transitive partial cubes of girth six
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a vertex-transitive partial cube, and suppose that its girth is six.

**Middle-level graph conjecture.** The graph $G$ is a middle-level graph.

The conjecture proposes that the known middle-level graphs exhaust the vertex-transitive partial cubes of girth six. The classification in the paper establishes the claim for the cases covered by its results, while the broader classification problem for higher-valency vertex-transitive partial cubes remains open.
